STEP 6 DONE (pure refactor). prepare_resume is split into consume_for_resume (still the one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal; returns resume::Consumed), released_call and build_segment. A thin prepare_resume composes consume_for_resume then build_segment, so the run_agent_with_route call site is unchanged (step 9 replaces it). The three Recorder.order assertions did not change. Consumed no longer needs any dead_code allow.

STEP 7 DONE. reserve_release is the one pre-reserve of the segment's first (seeded) round, before phase 2, in stage 1, whatever the release class, ledger on only. Created with the release dispatching sets prereserved and phase 2 skips the reserve for that action id but still finalizes. Created with the release rejected in phase 1 finalizes not_run at once. AlreadyReserved ends Err failed_precondition continuation_already_consumed before any dispatch, for every class. Err holds the release back (it is never run) with today's text, and the loop continues. The phase-2 entry predicate is now effectful-or-covered-by-release, the effects hold keeps class.is_effectful(), and BOTH the pre-reserve and phase 2 build their entry through effect::entry_for_call / LedgerEntry::new. The tool name is trimmed inside LedgerEntry::new, so one identity per action. Reserve errors, decided per case with evidence: session-core answers already_exists when the row is bound to different immutable input (checked in grpc.rs reserve_tool_action). effect::reserve now maps that to the new ReserveOutcome::IdentityConflict via the pure reserve_result. For the release that is a refusal with the closed token continuation_already_consumed and nothing dispatched. For an ordinary phase-2 call it keeps today's held-back behaviour. A reserve that errors or times out after it committed (reserve_commit_then_fail_for) is treated as an ambiguous transport error: in stage 1 the release is held back, never run, today's text, and the next attempt meets the committed row and ends continuation_already_consumed. In the in-place stage a failed pre-reserve is Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable, which is step 9 wiring: the Err arm in run_rounds is marked for it and there is no in-place branch yet. Tests (10): read release pre-reserved with class read and ordered reserve < dispatch < finalize; effectful release reserved once not twice; ledger off reserves nothing; same-claim replay with a read release runs ONE model loop (shared tier recorder, later-round effect reserved once, INV-02); phase-1-rejected release reserved then not_run, replay refused with no model loop; consent-gated (Ask) release fenced too; failed and commit-then-fail pre-reserve for a read and an effect keep the held-back text and the loop continues; identity conflict on the release refuses with nothing dispatched and nothing terminalized; identity conflict on an ordinary call still held back; the_release_and_the_dispatch_reserve_one_identity_for_the_same_call drives the REAL continuation path and the REAL phase-2 path and requires the recorded ReserveToolActionRequests equal field for field (only the action id differs, by the segment prefix). APPEND under the 2026-10-18 S7b v3 in-place resume rules entry (unit s7b-2, stage A: writer agreement, steps 6 to 8 and the Build 3a closeouts).

(2b) The two writer decisions agree by construction. FoldWriter::seeded forces gate.resumed to false itself (an in-place resume is never a stage-1 segment), and resume::in_place_writer_off does the same, so the pre-claim decision and the seeded writer cannot disagree whatever a caller put in resumed. The agreement test passes one unmodified gate to both over 384 combinations. A won claim followed by a fence the writer cannot write is therefore not reachable from the gate.

(3a) The release pre-reserve (reserve_release) runs in the segment's first round, before phase 2, ledger on only, in stage 1 now and in place at step 9. It is built by the same builder as a dispatch reservation (effect::LedgerEntry::new through entry_for_call and ApprovedRelease::ledger_entry; the tool name is trimmed in the builder). Phase 2 skips the reserve for the pre-reserved action and still finalizes it. A release the pre-pass rejected is reserved and finalized not_run at once.

(3b) Reserve answers, decided per case. Evidence: session-core reserve_tool_action answers created:false for an exact replay, already_exists when the action is bound to different immutable input, and any transport error may hide a commit.
- created:false: Err failed_precondition continuation_already_consumed before any dispatch, every class.
- already_exists (ReserveOutcome::IdentityConflict): the same refusal and token, nothing dispatched and no model loop; whatever holds the row is another attempt of this approval under another identity. For an ordinary phase-2 call it stays held back in today's words (it was an Err before).
- any other error or timeout, including one that committed: in stage 1 the release is held back and never run, with today's held-back text, and the loop continues; the next attempt meets the committed row and ends continuation_already_consumed. In place (step 9) it is a refusal, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, with nothing of the round dispatched.
The 'at most one model loop per approval' invariant holds for a read release too once the executor image that pre-reserves is deployed first (D10).

(3c) Operator signature for mismatch M1 (gateway resume on, executor ledger off): the executor warn line continue_replay_refused_ledger_off {run_id}, one per refused replay, ids only. It is the only change reachable with every switch off, and it is a log line on a path that already refuses with the same status.

(8) Content-bearing resume types (Consumed, ClaimedFold, Restored, SeedSlot) have a manual Debug that prints ids, counts, digests and closed tokens only, pinned by a test, so a {:?} of them can never put a call's arguments, a history or an outcome in a log or a failed assertion.

(9) Compose comments corrected: with AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED off the executor REFUSES a continue (continue_disabled) after the gateway has spent the click; it is not downgraded to a segment. A resume switch, ledger or fold writer off downgrades; the continue switch off loses the click. The model-gateway reader of EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED arrives with S7c-B.

findings.issue: classify_continue_dispatch_failure is spend-agnostic and its doc does not say so. It returns Refused for InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied from RunAgent. The design (regime 3) requires a continuation the gateway did NOT pre-consume to keep the committed terminalizing agent_dispatch_rejected arm for exactly those three codes. Nothing in this unit encodes or tests that split.
findings.evidence: The classify match arm groups FailedPrecondition | Aborted | InvalidArgument | PermissionDenied | Unauthenticated into Refused. The tests a_refused_continuation_is_classified_without_terminalizing and the REFUSAL_CARRIERS constant treat all five as refusals. The design's interfaces section says an unspent continuation refused with InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied takes the committed arm and terminalizes, and the 'switches off means byte-identical' rule depends on it. S7c-B1 must apply the split itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the classify doc that the caller must send InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied from an unspent (NotSpent) continuation to the committed rejection arm. Preferably add a small pure helper, for example classify_for(spend, &Status) -> Option<ContinueDispatchFailure>, plus a test, so B1 cannot get it wrong. At minimum, make B1's byte-identical-switch-off test cover an unspent InvalidArgument.

findings.issue: continue_refusal_event does not guard its own contract. The CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS doc says continue_unreachable and continue_outcome_unknown exist only with approval_spent, and the SPA treats them as spent-only. The function accepts those tokens with ApprovalSpend::NotSpent and emits them without the flag. Its debug_assert checks only vocabulary membership.
findings.evidence: continue_refusal_event("r","run","continue_outcome_unknown", ApprovalSpend::NotSpent) is accepted, and no test covers it. Only the spent-only wrappers (continue_failure_event, dispatch_unknown_event) pass SpentByGateway. The SPA contract CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_SPENT_ONLY_FRAME_REFUSALS says there is no unflagged form of these codes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add debug_assert!(spend.is_spent() || !matches!(token, "continue_unreachable" | "continue_outcome_unknown")). Add a should_panic test or a scan, and put the same list in a named const the BFF parity test can read.

findings.issue: approval_spend_for(resume_enabled) returns SpentByGateway from the switch alone, while the ApprovalSpend doc and the design invariant say the value is set only after a won consume, inside the launch closure. If B1 computes it before the consume and uses it for a frame on a path where the consume was lost or refused, the gateway would claim approval_spent when it spent nothing.
findings.evidence: The ApprovalSpend doc says 'set only after a consume that was won'. approval_spend_for contains `if resume_enabled { SpentByGateway }`, and its test pins only that mapping. No pure-piece test ties SpentByGateway to the won-consume path.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docs to say approval_spend_for names the regime and a frame may carry the flag only on the launch path after consume_then_launch returned Ok. B1 needs a test that a 409 or 503 before the stream carries no approval_spent. No code change is needed in this unit.

findings.issue: A zero-retention catalogue refusal on the consume (session-core refuse_zdr_continuation returns FailedPrecondition with the ZDR trailer) is mapped by preconsume_refusal to 409 not_resumable. The gateway's persistent gate refuses ZDR and waived turns before any consume, so it is defence in depth only.

With every Model Plane switch off the route answers the eight closed codes (continue_disabled, not_resumable, approval_not_found, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable, continuation_already_consumed, continue_unavailable) under the upstream status with the BFF's own fixed messages, where it used to answer model_error. A committed model-gateway with its continue switch off answers 409 continue_disabled, which the BFF now relays by that code. Accepted because no UI calls the route yet; pinned by orchestration.rs the_continue_relay_has_no_switch_and_names_closed_codes_with_every_model_plane_switch_off, which also scans that continue_run passes the list unconditionally. The relay also reads up to 4096 bytes of the error body, with a 5 s timeout, before answering; a read error, an oversized body or a stall means model_error. Unlike the other switches this one cannot be rolled back by flipping it: reverting it means passing &[] from continue_run.

What the SPA contract says about the spend (chat-run-continue-contract.ts): `no` is claimed only for approval_not_granted, approval_expired and approval_not_resumable, which are produced only for an unconsumed approval. continue_disabled, not_resumable and approval_not_found can answer a retry for a spent approval and are `unknown`; a transport failure (502 upstream_unavailable, 504, a network error, an unlisted body) is `unknown` and same-token-retryable. No read the SPA has shows whether an approval was spent, so the contract never asks a client to look at the approval: it says follow the run by its id with the existing run read, and a retry with the same token answers 409 continuation_already_consumed if the click was spent. After continue_unavailable that 409 can mean spent with no run launched; the run may be recovered inside the recovery window, about 15 minutes from the consume.

The gateway-parity half of the vocabulary test is still NOT written, as instructed. The deferred text from the previous report (build3a.json, unit s7c-a5, deferred_files) still applies unchanged and lands in the same commit as the S7c-A4 constants CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS and CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS. Until then the 22 stream tokens are pinned to no Rust source, and the SPA test header and the CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS doc comment now say so.

findings.issue: The new ambiguous-failure guidance contradicts the unit's own effect table. It says that resending with the same token, if the click was spent, "is answered 409 continuation_already_consumed, and otherwise it continues the run". The same unit reclassified not_resumable, continue_disabled and approval_not_found as unknown precisely because they can answer a retry for a SPENT approval. A client that follows the guidance literally, treating 409 continuation_already_consumed as spent and anything else as unspent and continuing, will misclassify a spent approval whose run has since ended. The registry description and the client doc repeat the loose version.
findings.evidence: CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_AMBIGUOUS_FAILURE_GUIDANCE is pinned verbatim by the test 'tells a client what it CAN do...'. continue_preflight in model-gateway sse.rs checks run status (not_resumable), then pairing (approval_not_found), then granted, and only then consumed. session-core consume_approval_with answers NotFound for a replay on an ended run (orchestration_store.rs, `mode.is_empty() || !run_keeps_state`). So after a spend plus a finished run, the retry answers 409 not_resumable or 404 approval_not_found, not continuation_already_consumed. 'Otherwise it continues' is also false: the retry can be refused approval_not_granted, approval_expired and so on.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the guidance and the registry/client text. A retry with the same token is answered either with the continuation or with a refusal. continuation_already_consumed means spent. not_resumable, approval_not_found and continue_disabled leave the spend unknown, and the run read is the arbiter. Update the pinned strings in the three tests to match.

findings.issue: The transport effect is retryable: true for every unlisted failure, including deterministic refusals that no retry can fix. That covers a 400 continue_incomplete or invalid_chat_request, 401 and 403 (a consume PermissionDenied, ZDR durable_mutation_forbidden) and 413/422. The class bundles genuinely transient failures (502 upstream_unavailable, 504, network, mid-stream envelope) with permanent ones under one retryable flag. A caller that trusts the flag can loop on a refusal that will never succeed. The spent value is also unknown for failures that provably happened before any consume.
findings.evidence: chatRunContinueTransportFailureOf returns transport('unlisted') for any status >= 400 that is not a 504. CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_TRANSPORT_EFFECT has retryable: true. The tests pin { code: 'continue_incomplete', status: 400 }, { code: 'unauthorized', status: 401 } and { code: 'missing_bearer', status: 401 } as retryable. model-gateway continuation_gate refuses ZDR with DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN, which the BFF turns into model_error under the same status. For a ZDR caller 'retry the same token, follow the run' can never succeed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make retryable true only for the reasons upstream_unavailable, gateway_timeout and network. Give 'unlisted' retryable false, keep spent unknown, and keep followRun true. Alternatively set retryable false for 400/401/403/413/422 and add tests.

findings.issue: The dropped-stream case that motivated the unit is read by no guard. continueRun resolves normally when the stream ends without a terminal frame, and also on a user abort, because readSseStream swallows AbortError. The contract says that between the two guards they read every failed request, which is not true for these cases. Nothing in the contract tells a caller that a clean close with no terminal frame, or an abort after the consume, is an ambiguous outcome (spent unknown, follow the run).
findings.evidence: sse.ts readSseStream: `if (done) break`, then the finally runs onDone and the promise resolves with no connError. `catch (err) { if (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'AbortError') return ... }`. continueRun only throws connError. The new tests cover thrown errors only, and the doc comment says 'a dropped connection' without covering a normal EOF.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the contract and in the continueRun doc that a stream that ends with no terminal frame, or is aborted after send, is the ambiguous case with the same effect as the transport failure. Better, add a typed guard or sentinel the caller can use, such as an 'ended without a terminal frame' result, with a test. Either way, drop the claim that the two guards read every failed request.

findings.issue: The 'existing run read' is left unnamed because the implementer reported that the SPA has no run-detail read. That is wrong. runs-client.ts exports getRun(runId), which calls GET /api/v1/agents/runs/{run_id}. The BFF route exists in agents_runs.rs, and RunDetail carries status and resumable. The guidance and the pinned tests keep the phrase 'the existing run read', which a client author cannot map to a function. A zero-retention or waived run, which gets not_resumable, has no readable run.
findings.evidence: grep of src/shared/api/runs-client.ts line ~175 'export async function getRun'. The deviation text in the report says 'The SPA has no run-detail read in orchestration-client, only the run-events replay'.
findings.suggested_fix: Name getRun in runs-client in the guidance and the registry description, and say a run that was never persisted cannot be read. Update the pinned strings and the stated deviation.

findings.issue: chatRunContinueTransportFailureOf classifies any object that has no numeric status and no error-like shape as a transport failure ('unlisted'), for example {} or an SSE frame object. Its own doc and the file header say a null from both guards means 'not a failed request at all', so a caller passing a non-error object gets a false 'failed request, spent unknown'.
findings.evidence: The function returns transport(errorLike ? 'network' : 'unlisted') after the status branch with no check that the object looks like a failure. The tests cover only non-objects, arrays and status < 400 for null.
findings.suggested_fix: Return null when there is no numeric status, no error.code envelope and no error-like shape, and add a test for {} and a frame-shaped object.

fix.summary:
The one finding is fixed. I checked it first and it was real. The old guidance said a same-token retry is answered "409 continuation_already_consumed, and otherwise it continues the run". The unit's own table says that is false for three codes:
- A spent approval whose run has ended can answer a retry with 409 not_resumable or 404 approval_not_found. A flipped-off switch gives 409 continue_disabled.
- A retry can also be refused approval_not_granted or approval_expired, so "otherwise it continues" was wrong in general.

The wording now says:
- A retry with the same token is "answered either with the continuation or with a refusal".
- "Only 409 continuation_already_consumed means the click was spent".
- not_resumable, approval_not_found and continue_disabled "leave the spend unknown", because a spent approval whose run has ended, or whose switch is off, gets them too.
- "The run read is the arbiter."

The same correction went into the following places:
- The pinned CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_AMBIGUOUS_FAILURE_GUIDANCE string.
- The chat.run.continue registry description, which now also lists approval_not_found among the codes a spent approval can get.
- The continueRun doc comment in the client.
- Three comments in the contract that carried the same loose "either the continuation or 409" claim: the `retryable` field doc, the continue_unavailable table row and the transport-effect doc.

Method:

deferred_files.content: After an ambiguous failure the SPA contract does not assume either way and says: follow the run by its id with the existing run read, which is the arbiter. A retry with the same claim token is answered either with the continuation or with a refusal. Only 409 continuation_already_consumed means the click was spent. not_resumable, approval_not_found and continue_disabled leave the spend unknown, because the gateway checks the switch, the run's state and the approval's pairing before it asks whether the approval was consumed, and the consume reports a replay on an ended run as not found. A client that treated 'not a 409 continuation_already_consumed' as 'unspent, so it continues' would misclassify a spent approval whose run had ended. After continue_unavailable a same-token 409 can mean spent with no run launched; the run may be recovered inside the recovery window, about 15 minutes from the consume.
